title: Elementary Continuity Axioms
summary: Elementary continuity axioms guarantee the line-circle and circle-circle intersections used in straightedge-and-compass constructions, but only under explicit crossing conditions.
statements: Line-circle continuity: if a line contains a point strictly inside a circle, then the line meets the circle in two distinct points.
Circle-circle continuity: if there are points P and Q on one circle such that P lies strictly inside another circle and Q lies strictly outside it, then the two circles meet in two distinct points.

historicalContext.title: Making construction assumptions explicit
paragraphs: Euclid's constructions sometimes introduce line-circle or circle-circle intersection points when the diagram suggests that they exist, without stating a general continuity principle that guarantees them. Later foundations made such existence assumptions explicit.

The elementary continuity axioms used here state only the two crossing principles needed for standard straightedge-and-compass constructions. They are narrower than full Dedekind or Hilbert completeness and do not assert that arbitrary lines or circles meet.

whatItEnables: You can justify construction steps that require a line or circle to cross a circle. These axioms do not claim that arbitrary lines or circles intersect.
